newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt/currency market closing report.

text.p: Yields ended higher and the crown was softer after an uneventful day on Monday, when trade was thin because U.S. and British markets were closed.

Yields opened higher on the results of the first round of the French parliamentary elections and dealers said they could rise more. "I think we will see a further rise in yields once the U.S. and British markets open tomorrow. The French results were a shock," one dealer said.
"It is hard to make anything out of the weakening since the market has been so thin. We will have to wait until tomorrow when London is open again," another dealer said.
The market was focussing on the second round of the French elections as well as on the long awaited announcement of the Swedish government's stance on EMU, due by the end of May.
Six month T-bill rate rose three basis points to 4.26 percent and the ten year bond yield rose seven basis points to 7.10 percent.
The crown weakened to 4.5115 crowns against the mark versus 4.4910 crowns on Friday.
